summary: The equation is of mixed type: hyperbolic, parabolic, elliptic in different regions.

methods.name: Discriminant test
methods.reason: The type of a second-order linear equation is decided by its second-order coefficients alone.

steps.title: Compute the discriminant
steps.text: For \(A u_{xx} + B u_{xy} + C u_{yy} + \cdots = 0\) the type depends only on the sign of \(B^2 - 4AC\). Lower-order terms do not matter.

steps.title: Read off the type
steps.text: The discriminant changes sign, so the type depends on the point: hyperbolic where it is positive, parabolic where it is zero, elliptic where it is negative.

steps.title: Find the characteristics
steps.text: Characteristics are the curves along which information travels. They solve the ordinary differential equation below. They are real only in the region where the discriminant is not negative.

steps.title: Canonical form
steps.text: A change of variables built from the characteristics brings the second-order part to a standard shape. Where it is hyperbolic it behaves like the wave equation (two families of real characteristics). Where it is parabolic it behaves like the heat equation (one family of real characteristics). Where it is elliptic it behaves like Laplace's equation (no real characteristics).

steps.title: Type
latex: \text{mixed type: }\text{hyperbolic where } y < 0;\ \text{parabolic where } y = 0;\ \text{elliptic where } 0 < y
